source_quality.equation_authority: text layer, running footer corrupts many lines

task_reconstruction.official_task: 2024 MCM Problem C, momentum in a tennis match, addressed to coaches and players.
required_outputs: a definition of momentum from the recent games and points
a way to mark the swings
a test of whether the swings are random
the factors most tied to the swings
a memo to coaches and players

section_map.summary: abstract: the average, the test, the network, the failure on women's matches
introduction: the stronger player loses, then the dispute
data: one filled value, then a reduction to three
model-establishment: two scales and a sigmoid
model-establishment: three networks and an upset
sensitivity: the step and the cluster count
limitations: the concession and the failed transfer

contributions.summary: The game score is a sigmoid, defended by the gap between winning at 67 percent and losing at 33.
The filter is chosen by burying the other three for named faults.
The swings fail a randomness test and pass a reading against two breaks of serve.
The network that was expected to win does so only after training on similar matches.

dependency_graph.label: The curve is smoothed and differentiated.
The momentum is the training target.
The networks are retrained on the nearest cluster.
The labeled swings are what the tree attributes.

assumptions.summary: No suspension, and the changeover follows the rule book.
Both players are committed, and the head-to-head record is ignored.
The mental state comes only from scoring, running, and condition.
Earlier rounds left the same exertion on everyone.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Men's matches after the first two rounds. One serve speed filled by interpolation inside its own game, printed as 115 mph.
Spearman correlation first, then the reduction. The two running distances collapse, and the ten columns become three.
The figures are read down to a unit: sets, then games.

models.summary: MU-C-Q248-001: a two-scale weighted average with a sigmoid game score.
MU-C-Q248-002: a wavelet filter and a curvature rule at 0.03.
MU-C-Q248-003: three recurrent networks on one structure.
MU-C-Q248-004: transfer from the nearest of three clusters.
MU-C-Q248-005: boosted trees read by average gain.

verification.summary: Points 68 and 296, each a break of serve.
Test loss 0.2, close to the training loss.
Step 10 to 15 recommended. Three clusters best.

results_trace.summary: Djokovic represses the first set and the curves lock in the second.
GRU and RNN beat LSTM before the transfer.
Distance run ranks first, then the game numbers, then the serve.
The women's matches diverge, and the paper says the transfer was inappropriate.

writing_logic.summary: The quantity arrives only after the score has been shown to fail.
The test and the counterexample are both kept, each with its condition.
The failed expectation is written down and then allowed to change the method.
The weakness section concedes that the model is not convincing.
The memo directs the reader back to the paper.

visualization_observations.summary: A flowchart of the reading, captioned as the train of thoughts.
A ten by ten correlation heatmap, blue for positive and green for negative.
Games won per match, and the point difference per game, dot size for the gap and color for the frequency.
The line against the sigmoid, the gap between 33 and 67 percent opened up.
The weighting scheme as balls, the darkest furthest from the current point.
The final, green for Djokovic and blue for Alcaraz, read against the five set scores.
Four filters, green circles on the stretches that failed.
The first difference with the swings in blue, and a warning about labeling integers.
The shared network, three hidden layers.
Three forecasts against one true curve.
Two training orders, one row each.
The training and test losses after transfer.
The factor ranking, distance at the top.
Step size against accuracy, two bars per step.
The deviation against the cluster count, and the three clusters in space.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The paper prints both the test that says random and the two points that say otherwise, so the disagreement stays visible.
The expectation that LSTM would win is stated before the figure that shows it losing.

weaknesses.summary: The momentum at a point uses games that have not yet been played.
The run test is read as evidence of randomness and the prose argues the contrary.
SHAP is named but the ranking is described as average gain, and no gain is numbered.
The model fails on women's matches and on volleyball, and says so.

independent_extensions.summary: Rebuild the game baseline so it uses only games already played, which the printed window does not.
Read the factor ranking from the SHAP values the heading promises, instead of the average gain the prose reports.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Let the counterexample follow the test immediately.
Bury each rejected option with the fault the figure shows.

unresolved_questions: How is the five-game window filled at the start and end of a match?
What gain does each factor actually have?
Which of the four transfer options in the code produced the loss of 0.2?
